review_context: Rust leaf-tool slice adding deterministic snapshot coherence for checked UI fixture manifests.
finding_title: Checked demo fixture manifests can drift from current local JSON fixtures without a deterministic gate.
finding_summary: The checked read-only UI demo manifest can become stale when source fixture JSON files change. This slice adds a Rust-backed, candidate-only snapshot coherence report that compares the expected manifest against the current fixture tree and fails closed on changed, missing, or unexpected JSON files.
observable_context: The existing Rust fixture manifest scanner emits stable file hashes for local JSON fixtures.
The checked demo manifest currently reports 23 expected files.
Running the new snapshot coherence command against the checked demo fixture root produced status=failed with 21 matched files, 2 changed files, 0 missing files, and 0 unexpected files.
A read-only subagent separately observed stale UI review data bundle source hashes, which remains an adjacent next-slice gate.
Full validation after the implementation passed with 643 tests and the smoke demo ended at blocked_pending_conflicts_and_engagement.
observable_decision_logic: Fixture generation and fixture verification are separate claims.
A drift checker must not auto-repair checked fixtures because that would collapse evidence detection into evidence mutation.
Changed, missing, and unexpected fixture files are different exception labels and should be visible to DAD for pattern analysis.
The first Rust gate should stay path/hash/count based; semantic UI bundle hash validation should remain a separate follow-up.
solution_path: Add the fixture_snapshot_coherence Rust binary beside the existing boundary checker and manifest scanner.
Add a Python wrapper and CLI command named build-rust-fixture-snapshot-coherence-report.
Add Pydantic report models and exported JSON schemas for the new candidate-only report.
Add focused tests proving clean snapshots pass and changed, missing, and unexpected fixture drift fails closed.
Document the tool as a detector only, with no fixture regeneration, Lake write, SQLite write, budget submission, matter opening, or silent learning.
applies_when: A checked read-only UI fixture manifest is used as evidence for current local JSON fixture state.
A generated demo report is copied or left stale after source fixtures change.
A review dashboard or DAD workflow needs to distinguish current fixture state from historical checked evidence.
does_not_apply_when: The manifest is explicitly historical and is not being used as evidence of current fixture state.
The artifact being checked is non-JSON or outside the local fixture/report tree.
A stronger owner-approved runtime artifact registry already supplies the current hash-bound evidence.
danger_if_misapplied: If this gate is treated as a fixture refresh tool, it may hide the very drift it is meant to expose. If ignored, stale demo evidence can create false readiness or inaccurate DAD learning signals.
suggested_actions: DAD should classify manifest drift separately from UI review data bundle source-hash drift.
DAD should treat the new report as a concrete candidate Exception Lake event shape for checked-evidence drift.
Codex should add the separate UI bundle source-hash coherence gate before claiming the read-only UI demo bundle is fully current.
reviewer_notes: This record contains synthetic fixture and local artifact references only.
It records observable evidence, decision logic, fix refs, and test refs without hidden chain-of-thought.
red_team_notes: Do not auto-regenerate checked UI fixtures inside the drift gate.
Do not treat snapshot coherence as production readiness, calibration, budget approval, matter opening, or Lake admission.
Do not promote local candidate report schemas to Semantic Substrate canon from this repo.
